key_insight: EndoCoT enables Multimodal LLMs to perform endogenous, multi-step Chain-of-Thought reasoning inside the diffusion denoising loop, producing evolving guidance rather than a single static encoding—leading to deeper, task-specific reasoning for complex multimodal tasks.
problem_solved: Addresses two core limitations of current MLLM+diffusion pipelines: (1) single-step text encoding fails to trigger Chain-of-Thought reasoning, and (2) guidance from the MLLM remains invariant across diffusion steps, limiting complex spatial and compositional reasoning.
method: Introduce EndoCoT: activate internal CoT states within the MLLM that are iteratively updated and conditioned on during diffusion denoising.
Couple evolving MLLM reasoning outputs with diffusion steps so guidance adapts over time instead of staying fixed.
Adopt scaling strategies (e.g., stepwise conditioning and training procedures to stabilize long-form internal reasoning) to make endogenous CoT practical in large diffusion workflows.
impact: Provides a practical way to get deeper, dynamic reasoning from MLLMs in diffusion-based multimodal systems, improving accuracy on spatial/compositional tasks and enabling richer model guidance for downstream applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing a diffusion model loop with the MLLM producing evolving Chain-of-Thought tokens at multiple denoising steps (contrast with single-step static guidance).
Before/After comparison: static guidance vs. EndoCoT dynamic guidance on a spatial reasoning example (annotations showing corrections across steps).
Performance bar chart or table summarizing gains on representative benchmarks (e.g., spatial/compositional tasks).
Schematic highlighting scaling techniques (stepwise conditioning & training flow) that enable stable endogenous CoT.
paper_title: EndoCoT: Scaling Endogenous Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Xuanlang Dai, Yujie Zhou, Long Xing, Jiazi Bu, Xilin Wei
